description: Notes from the bench: what I measured, what broke and what I would do differently.

items.content_html: I made a Spring endpoint nine times faster this week. The way I did it is by skipping most of what Spring does to keep you safe.
items.title: 5,800 to 53,000 req/s by skipping the filter chain

items.content_html: At work I would never accept a system without a tested, off-site backup. At home I ran one for years, and it held everything I actually care about.
items.title: 661 backups and none of them off-site

items.content_html: 'We sent it correctly.' I have heard that sentence many times, and most of the time I could not check it.
items.title: A gateway that logs every body

items.content_html: Recording every request body costs my new gateway about a third of its throughput. I think that is cheap.
items.title: A gateway that remembers every request

items.content_html: I rooted my printer, changed its config, and then got annoyed when a firmware update did not respect my changes.
items.title: A K2 firmware update deletes your config and your root

items.content_html: Everybody knows you should not build a message queue on a database. I just did, and I think it was the right call.
items.title: A Kafka-like queue on MySQL

items.content_html: I want to know where users are, and I do not want to know where users are.
items.title: A map tile as a 64-bit integer

items.content_html: I have a plasma TV and a Chromecast, and they do not like each other.
items.title: A screen saver for a Chromecast, to save a plasma TV

items.content_html: I like profilers. I also cannot use one where I need it most, which is in production, on the request that is slow right now.
items.title: A stopwatch you can leave on in production

items.content_html: We built it in about an hour. Agreeing on what to build took most of the day.
items.title: A study buddy that refuses to give the answer

items.content_html: I thought that since it feels pretty late to enter the blogosphere at my age, I will write up a small explanation, if there is anyone interested.
items.title: Back to the world

items.content_html: I spent a month putting balanced ventilation into our house, and I made the job about twice as big as it needed to be. On purpose.
items.title: Balanced ventilation in a house from 2000, with no visible ducts

items.content_html: The extra ducts paid off. Balancing the ventilation was simple.
items.title: 44 watts for 200 m³/h: balancing the ventilation myself

items.content_html: I’m happy to announce version 2.6.2 of eclipselink-maven-plugin!
items.title: eclipselink-maven-plugin 2.6.2 released

items.content_html: On 18 September I filed five bugs against my own gateway. I had not found any of them myself. An AI review did, in code I have run since 2023.
items.title: Five bugs in my own gateway in one day

items.content_html: For some time I have meant to fully document all the different APIs I’m involved in. It gives a more professional feel, it helps integrators and front-end developers and it actually makes it…
items.title: Generic API documenter for web-services

items.content_html: In May I imported the world into MySQL. In October I deleted the database, and the library got simpler.
items.title: Geo lookups without a database

items.content_html: This page was created to try to distill the information from more than 5,000 forum posts.
items.title: NVIDIA GTX 970 overclocking

items.content_html: In September 2026 I spent three days making a date parser faster. It already took less than a microsecond.
items.title: Parsing ISO-8601 21 to 67 times faster than java.time

items.content_html: Everyone is moving from XML to JSON. I just wrote a tool that goes the other way.
items.title: JSON Schema to XSD
